turns.text: A long time ago. Back then I felt like it was a normal part of marriage—like you do stupid stuff and you get yelled at, you don’t really care, you move on. Then I realized how awful it was and I ran.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: Thank you for saying that. What happened then after you left?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I got into therapy because I was so depressed after the abuse. I didn't have the words to say it, but my therapist told me I was a victim of domestic violence.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: I'm really sorry that happened. Are you safe now, and do you have support in place if contact ever shows up?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I'm safe now. I just keep thinking back to his "I was wrong," but I'm so used to being abused that I can't shake it. I don't know what to do. I want him out of my life, but I don't want to be alone.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: It makes sense to be torn. You deserve to be safe and be heard. Do you have a plan for staying away and for support if he reaches out?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I mostly want him out of my life. I don’t want to be single. I don’t know if I can just block him forever without feeling guilty. I keep doubting myself.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: Your feelings matter, and you don’t owe him anything after what happened. It’s okay to block or avoid contact for your safety. You can also set boundaries with friends and family to keep space, and lean on your therapist or a trusted person.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I keep thinking if I stay single it'll feel like I failed. But I also know I deserve better. I'm just scared of being alone.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: Feeling alone can feel like failure, but it doesn’t have to be the only story. You’re not failing—trauma can make us feel isolated and unworthy. You can also focus on building a support system, therapy, and small, grounding habits to help with the loneliness.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: Thanks for hearing me. I'm going to try to block him and focus on myself. I still feel torn, but I think that's okay.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: That’s a strong and protective step. You’re allowed to choose your path, and you deserve care and safety. If it ever gets overwhelming, please reach out again—I’m here.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: Hi. I just wanted to vent. I've been a huge fan of your work for ages, but I can't take it anymore. It feels like every story you tell is about trauma. It's draining and honestly, I want a break from the heavy stuff.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way. I hear how exhausting it can be to keep absorbing so much trauma-focused storytelling. Are you talking about specific stories or just the overall tone and frequency?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: It's been building. Every time I finish a story, I just want to feel something other than sadness, fear, or pain. It's like your work is all about pain and I just want a change. Maybe I just needed a break.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: That sounds really draining. When the sadness or fear hits, does it spike your anxiety or just take you down? And do you have space to step back from the stories while you recharge?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I just want some stories that give me hope or something good. Maybe stories that are less intense. It would mean a lot if I could take a break, even just for a bit.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: Absolutely. You can choose where and when you watch, and set limits. If the intensity spikes, a short pause is okay. What helps you get out of the heavy mood—music, walks, a show that feels gentle?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I love your work and I still want to support it, but I need a pause. I can't keep taking on this much trauma in my head day after day.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: That makes sense. You don't owe anyone your mental energy for a season. You're allowed to step back and care for yourself. Would you like to try a gentle approach for the next few days, like limiting sessions or choosing lighter content when it feels right?

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: Yeah, maybe. I need to put some distance. It's all the trauma and I just need a break.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: Good. Maybe start by setting a time limit and picking content that feels lighter, then check in with yourself and adjust. You can also reach out to others for support while you do.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I appreciate that. I need a bit of space to breathe.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: You're welcome. I'm glad you spoke up. If the break helps, we can revisit later—your comfort comes first.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: Thank you. I'll take a pause and see how I feel.

turns.speaker: Listener
turns.text: You're taking care of yourself, and that's what matters. If anything changes or you want to talk more later, I'm here. Take care.

turns.speaker: User
turns.text: I appreciate it. Thank you for listening.
